audit.whatIsWrong: Every full-layer phases[N].side reads 'Skill' (flat/even) for all 7 rows, while content win[0-6] and packet.levelChart both say Swain wins rows 0-4 and Xayah wins rows 5-6 — the packet even flags this exact contradiction as a defect.
audit.why: Swain's early W root (Nevermove) plus Q (Death's Hand) poke and R (Demonic Ascension) drain sustain win the lane phase per the kit; Xayah's crit/Deadly Plumage scaling flips it once she has an item. This matches both packet.levelChart and content win[N], so full-layer side was the stale layer.
audit.corrected: Flipped phases[0-4].side to Swain and phases[5-6].side to Xayah to agree with win[N]; rewrote phases[0-4].why (previously written as if Xayah won) to state the Swain-favored reasons grounded in his kit. phases[5-6].why already matched the Xayah-favored verdict, so left untouched.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Demonic Ascension as matchup-defining but never gives its cooldown.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension (R) is a 120s cooldown — a single number that tells the reader exactly how rare the safe engage window is.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d are the tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted verbatim under unrelated titles ('R the rotation, then call the storm' / 'Dive the nest without the R') instead of describing what those titles actually promise.
audit.why: The Do's/Don'ts bullets should each stand on their own; the pasted content describes generic auto-trading and feather-call impatience, not the R-timing behavior the titles name.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both bodies to match their titles: baiting Demonic Ascension before committing, and reserving Featherstorm for his W pull-in rather than chip poke.

notes: The main defect here was the packet-flagged level-chart contradiction: full-layer phases[0-6].side were all flat 'Skill' while content win[N] and the packet chart agreed Swain wins rows 0-4 and Xayah wins 5-6. Content whys[0-4] already described Swain winning early (root/poke/drain), so I used those as the grounding for the rewritten full-layer why text rather than inventing new claims — the two layers should now read the same story. Ratings for the flipped Swain rows were raised from the flat 5-6/10 to 6-7/10 to reflect a real (not marginal) early Swain advantage; ratings are enum-exempt.
